stories.title: UKIPO announces changes to patent services
Forbes Solicitors announces 20 staff promotions
stories.ltme_summary: Forbes Solicitors has promoted 20 staff across its public sector, commercial and private client divisions, including new partners Rebecca McCann, Daniel Fletcher and Nicola Rushton. Managing Partner Pauline Wild welcomed the promotions. The announcement is firm-issued and covers partner, senior associate and associate levels.
stories.hook: Forbes Solicitors announces 20 promotions, including three new partners

stories.title: Managing AI-generated subject access requests
stories.ltme_summary: Solicitors Journal discusses how solicitors should handle subject access requests drafted with AI, citing ICO guidance published on 11 November. The guidance holds that AI assistance does not remove the right, so a request can stay valid despite inaccurate legal citations. The piece advises early routing to access teams and written search plans.
stories.hook: ICO guidance says AI-drafted subject access requests remain valid despite inaccurate legal citations

stories.title: NY Judges Warn AI Misconduct Bill Could Chill Judicial Independence
stories.hook: New York judges warn an AI misconduct bill could threaten judicial independence
entities: New York Supreme Court justices association

stories.title: How the Cyberthreat Facing Law Firms Is Changing
stories.ltme_summary: Legal Tech Monitor reports that cyber criminals targeting law firms are increasingly using the sensitivity of stolen information to pressure victims, rather than simply locking them out of systems. The item is a short aggregator summary with no named firms or incidents in the extract.
stories.hook: Cyber attackers targeting law firms now exploit stolen data sensitivity, not just system lockouts

Massachusetts No-Fault PIP Rules After a Boston Car Accident
$200bn and counting: Global 100 revenues more than double in a decade
stories.ltme_summary: Legal Business reports that the Global 100 law firms reached combined turnover of $200bn in 2025-26, with revenue more than doubling over ten years. Ninety-nine of the 100 firms grew, and more than half posted double-digit increases. The article is the magazine's own analysis of the annual ranking data.
stories.hook: Global 100 law firms reach $200bn combined turnover, with 99 of 100 growing in 2025-26

stories.title: Global 100 2026: Main table
stories.ltme_summary: Legal Business has published its Global 100 2026 main table of the largest law firms by revenue, with key financial metrics. The page is a data table and its headline page lists related rankings coverage, including the LB100 2026 series. The extract gives no individual firm figures.
stories.hook: Legal Business publishes its Global 100 2026 table of the world's largest law firms

stories.title: Dentons and Pinsents on call as Poundland collapses into administration
Ruth McLain appointed as Chair of ILFM Council
stories.ltme_summary: The Institute of Legal Finance & Management has appointed Ruth McLain ILFM (Dip) as Council chair after its AGM on 26 November, succeeding Victoria Williams. Jenny Bendrey becomes Vice Chair. McLain has more than 40 years' experience in legal cashiering, finance and compliance and will serve a two-year term.
stories.hook: Ruth McLain takes over as Chair of the Institute of Legal Finance & Management

stories.title: Leading, not following: Why Shepherd & Co. does things differently
stories.ltme_summary: Legal Futures, with Dye & Durham as associate, profiles Shepherd & Co., a seven-person firm in Towcester. Partners Sajid Nazir and Jabeer Ali Miah say they pay no referral fees and do not price-match. The firm uses Dye & Durham's legal cashiering service and practice management system for its accounts.
stories.hook: Towcester firm Shepherd & Co. refuses referral fees and price matching, relying on Dye & Durham

stories.title: Referral relationships are valuable: Is the way you manage them keeping pace?
stories.ltme_summary: Perfect Portal, writing as a Legal Futures associate, argues that law firms need better management of referral relationships after the lead is sent. It recommends simple submission processes, a central view of incoming referrals and consistent partner communication, and says technology can help. The piece is promotional content from a vendor.
stories.hook: Perfect Portal says firms must manage referral work after the lead, not just win it

stories.title: MLT Digital offers law firms a free practice area review as Google clicks for legal services fall
stories.hook: MLT Digital says practice-area search clicks to law firm websites fell 35.8 per cent in summer 2026

stories.title: Building sustainable legal careers in the age of AI: Why the human touch still matters
stories.ltme_summary: Osprey Approach's Empowering Law Firm Leaders podcast, episode 39, features Helen Barry, director and head of property at Watkins & Gunn Solicitors. She discusses alternative qualification routes, developing junior lawyers as AI changes training, and using AI and automation in conveyancing. She argues technology should enhance rather than replace the human side of legal work.
stories.hook: Helen Barry of Watkins & Gunn argues AI should enhance legal services, not replace the human touch

stories.title: OneAdvanced IQ: Make work flow
stories.ltme_summary: OneAdvanced, writing as a Legal Futures associate, promotes its IQ system of work, launched earlier in 2026. It groups the offer into an Intelligent Platform, Intelligent Workflows and Intelligent Services, and cites ISO 27001 and ISO 42001 certification. The piece is vendor marketing for a platform aimed at organisations generally.
stories.hook: OneAdvanced promotes IQ, its system of work spanning platform, workflows and services

stories.hook: LexisNexis Bellwether Report finds 62 per cent of small firms have grown in three to four years

stories.title: Startup Corner: Lexilio takes aim at construction’s hidden contract risks
stories.ltme_summary: Legal IT Insider's Startup Corner profiles Lexilio, which targets hidden contract risks in construction. The extract is only a bot-check page, so the product details and funding are not visible. The headline indicates the startup is a legal technology company focused on construction contracts.
stories.hook: Lexilio aims to surface hidden contract risks in construction, according to Legal IT Insider

Mishcon de Reya revenue rises 13% to £372m
No AML carveout for solicitors on FCA switch
stories.ltme_summary: Economic secretary to the Treasury Lucy Rigby told MPs during debate on the Financial Services and Markets Bill that the government does not signal any carve-out for solicitors from the transfer of AML oversight from the SRA to the FCA. She said the SRA will work with the FCA to minimise burden, particularly for smaller practices.
stories.hook: Treasury minister gives no sign solicitors will be carved out of FCA anti-money laundering oversight

stories.title: Complaints continuing to rise in most areas of law
stories.ltme_summary: Legal Services Board papers show OLC chair Richard Blakeway told LSB chair Monisha Shah that complaints are concentrated in a few firms. Motor insurance complaints roughly doubled in the second quarter and half relate to one firm. The ombudsman expects over 21,000 complaints in 2027/28 and proposes a budget of £22.8m, up 6.9 per cent.
stories.hook: Legal Ombudsman expects more than 21,000 complaints in 2027/28 and proposes £22.8m budget

stories.title: New coalition of 'champions' calls for expansion of problem-solving courts
stories.ltme_summary: The FDAC Champions initiative has launched to press for the family drug and alcohol court model to be rolled out nationally with sustained funding. The Gazette reports only 14 FDACs operate, serving 37 local authorities, and that teams lack permanent funding. It cites research showing 50 per cent of children are returned home under FDAC, against 13 per cent in standard proceedings.
stories.hook: FDAC Champions campaign calls for national rollout of family drug and alcohol courts

stories.title: Government backs anti-SLAPP bill
stories.ltme_summary: The Law Society Gazette reports the government backed John Whittingdale's SLAPPs (No. 2) Bill, which passed second reading unanimously in the Commons after 15 speeches. The bill creates a three-stage SLAPP definition and early dismissal, and would give defendants costs protection. It now goes to committee stage.
stories.hook: Commons approves anti-SLAPP bill at second reading, with government backing

stories.title: Costs protections in SLAPP bill do not go far enough, says justice committee
stories.ltme_summary: The Commons justice committee has written to minister Sarah Sackman asking government and the SRA to consider more prescriptive rules on solicitors' threats and misleading legal claims in correspondence. It says the SLAPPs bill's costs protections do not go far enough, ahead of the bill's Commons debate. The letter follows a 17 November evidence session.
stories.hook: Commons justice committee says SLAPP costs protections do not go far enough

stories.title: New protections will stop powerful figures silencing scrutiny
stories.ltme_summary: The Ministry of Justice says new Private Member's Bill, the SLAPPs Bill sponsored by Sir John Whittingdale MP and backed by government, would extend anti-SLAPP protection beyond economic crime cases to all public interest reporting. It would add a statutory SLAPP definition and early dismissal, and limit costs against unsuccessful defendants. Sarah Sackman KC MP is quoted.
stories.hook: Government backs SLAPPs Bill extending anti-SLAPP protection to all public interest reporting

Failure to record delivery: statutory notices in the Court of Appeal
stories.ltme_summary: RPC reports that the Court of Appeal, by a majority of two to one, dismissed a landlord's appeal in London Borough of Enfield v Lamba [2026] EWCA Civ 1485, decided on 20 November 2026. The court held that contractual service provisions displace statutory deemed service of a section 25 notice sent by recorded delivery that was returned undelivered. Nugee LJ dissented. The firm says the reasoning may affect other statutory notices.
stories.hook: Court of Appeal in Enfield v Lamba: contractual service terms can displace statutory deemed service

stories.title: Court of Appeal Clarifies Liability for Bulk-Metered Electricity Supplies
stories.ltme_summary: Shakespeare Martineau reports that the Court of Appeal in SmartestEnergy Business Ltd v Odeon Arcade Ltd [2026] EWCA Civ 1412 held a property owner liable under a statutory deemed electricity contract for a Leicester arcade served by one bulk meter, even though its retail units were let to tenants. SmartestEnergy sought £106,914.25 and had presented a winding-up petition. The court reversed two lower rulings, which had placed liability on the occupiers.
stories.hook: Court of Appeal puts bulk-meter electricity liability on owners, not tenants, in SmartestEnergy v Odeon Arcade

stories.title: From leasehold to commonhold: the coming revolution in homeownership
stories.ltme_summary: Trowers & Hamlins argues that the Commonhold and Leasehold Reform Bill would reset homeownership in England and Wales. Under the Bill, commonhold would replace most new leasehold flats, with a proposed ban, penalties of up to £30,000 and a 50 per cent leaseholder consent threshold for conversion. The firm expects wide effects on developers, lenders and managing agents.
stories.hook: Trowers & Hamlins: commonhold Bill would reset homeownership and ban most new leasehold flats

Syntheia Product Update: November 2026
stories.ltme_summary: Syntheia's November 2026 product update lists new features. PDF files can now be compared against Word files or other PDFs, producing a formatted redlined DOCX. Comparisons open in Claude or ChatGPT, Microsoft 365 mailboxes connect to email-in via OAuth, and the MCP server now handles source files, headings and layout. The update is published by the vendor on its own site.
stories.hook: Syntheia adds PDF-to-Word blacklining and native Microsoft 365 email-in in November update
